beats.say: A penny gets you a whole library. And the bill arrives later.
Sign up, get twelve records for a penny.
Then you must buy a set number of albums at regular price.
If you stay silent, the next record ships with a full-price invoice.
Revenue hit $1.4 billion in 1996, then $17 million by 2014. Looks absurd.
But it does a job: the penny is a trap.
The hidden clause forces a later purchase, turning a penny into ongoing revenue.
That clause kept shipments flowing until bankruptcy in 2015.
You see it everywhere: a gym offers a free month, then auto-renews at $49.
The cheap entry feels harmless, so the paid plan looks like a smart upgrade.
Watch the fine print before the penny. Follow for more.
